title: 第十五章 古寺藏凶煞刃破万重迷第十六章 西凉遇故知剑下辨忠奸
content_zh:
暮秋的风卷着山枯叶，在崎岖的山径上打旋，萧琰勒住缰绳，胯下的青鬃马不安地刨着蹄子，鼻息里喷吐着白气，目光警惕地望向密林深处。前方云雾缭绕，隐约可见飞檐翘角刺破雾霭，那便是灵泉寺——一座隐于苍梧山深处，荒废了十余年的古寺。
他此行，是为了追查三个月前失踪的御史李大人。据最后见过李大人的樵夫所言，大人一行五人，便是循着灵泉寺的方向进山，此后便杳无音信。官府曾派人搜山，却只在山脚下发现了半块染血的官袍碎片，以及一枚刻着“灵泉”二字的铜令牌，再无其他线索。更诡异的是，搜山的差役中，有两人莫名失踪，余下的人也皆面色惨白，声称夜里听到古寺方向传来凄厉的哭声，还看到黑影在林间穿梭，再也不敢深入半步。
萧琰抬手拢了拢腰间的软剑，剑鞘是玄铁所制，刻着细密的云纹，握在手中微凉。他自幼习武，又在刑部任职数年，见过无数凶案现场，却从未像此刻这般，被山间的阴冷气息压得心头发沉。苍梧山本就山高林密，入秋后更是荒无人烟，唯有风穿过树叶的“沙沙”声，夹杂着远处不知名鸟兽的低鸣，更显寂寥可怖。
“驾。”萧琰轻喝一声，拍了拍马颈，青鬃马虽仍有惧意，却还是顺从地踏着枯叶，缓缓向云雾深处行去。越靠近灵泉寺，雾气便越浓重，能见度不足丈余，空气中渐渐弥漫开一股怪异的气味——既有潮湿的霉味，又有淡淡的檀香，还夹杂着一丝若有若无的血腥气，三者交织在一起，令人作呕。
约莫半个时辰后，灵泉寺的山门终于出现在眼前。山门是青石砌成，高三丈有余，顶端的琉璃瓦早已斑驳脱落，露出底下灰暗的青砖，两侧的石狮子也残缺不全，一只缺了头颅，一只断了前爪，狰狞的面目在雾气中更显阴森。山门上方的“灵泉寺”三个大字，是用朱砂书写，如今朱砂大半剥落，只剩下模糊的轮廓，仿佛被岁月和某种诡异的力量侵蚀殆尽。
萧琰翻身下马，将马拴在山门旁的老槐树上，那老槐树早已枯死，枝干扭曲如鬼爪，缠绕着干枯的藤蔓，像是无数双伸出的手，要将人拖拽入黑暗之中。他抬手推了推山门，“吱呀——”一声悠长而刺耳的声响，打破了山间的寂静，这声音在空旷的山谷中回荡，竟带着几分哭腔，听得人头皮发麻。山门并未上锁，只是被厚厚的蛛网和灰尘封住，一推之下，灰尘簌簌落下，夹杂着几只受惊的黑蜘蛛，仓皇逃窜。
踏入山门的那一刻，一股刺骨的寒意扑面而来，与山间的秋风截然不同，这寒意带着几分阴邪，仿佛能穿透衣物，冻入骨髓。萧琰下意识地握紧了腰间的软剑，目光警惕地扫视着四周。山门内是一个开阔的庭院，地面上铺满了厚厚的枯叶和杂草，几株枯败的古柏伫立在庭院两侧，枝干斜斜地伸向天空，像是在无声地控诉。庭院中央有一座石香炉，炉身布满了裂痕，里面早已没有香火，只剩下一些发黑的灰烬，灰烬中隐约可见几片破碎的布料，颜色暗沉，像是染过血。
庭院的尽头，是灵泉寺的主殿——大雄宝殿。大殿的门扉虚掩着，门板上的红漆早已剥落，露出底下的木质纹理，上面布满了抓痕，像是被什么尖利的东西反复抓挠过。殿檐下的灯笼早已腐朽，只剩下残破的骨架，在风中轻轻摇晃，发出“哗啦哗啦”的声响，像是亡魂的低语。
萧琰放缓脚步，一步一步地走向大雄宝殿，脚下的枯叶被踩得“咔嚓”作响，在寂静的庭院中格外清晰。他每走一步，都能感觉到空气中的阴邪气息愈发浓重，那股血腥气也变得更加清晰，似乎就来自大雄宝殿之中。走到殿门口，他停下脚步，侧耳倾听，殿内一片死寂，没有任何声响，却又仿佛有无数双眼睛在暗处盯着他，让他浑身汗毛倒竖。
他深吸一口气，抬手轻轻推开了殿门。“吱呀——”又是一声刺耳的声响，殿内的光线瞬间变得昏暗，只有几缕阳光透过殿顶的破洞，斜斜地照进来，照亮了空气中飞舞的灰尘。萧琰适应了片刻，才渐渐看清了殿内的景象。
大雄宝殿内，正中的释迦牟尼佛像早已残缺不全，佛头不翼而飞，身躯上布满了裂痕，双手也断了一只，只剩下空荡荡的袖管，仿佛在无声地哭泣。佛像前的香案上，摆放着三个残破的香炉，里面积满了灰尘，香案上还散落着几枚锈蚀的铜钱和半支断裂的蜡烛。殿内的墙壁上，原本绘制着精美的壁画，如今却被涂抹得面目全非，只剩下一些模糊的线条，隐约能看出是佛经中的场景，只是那些人物的面容都被涂抹成了狰狞的模样，眼神诡异，仿佛要从墙壁中走出来一般。
萧琰的目光缓缓扫过殿内，忽然注意到佛像的底座下，有一丝暗红色的痕迹，像是干涸的血迹。他快步走过去，蹲下身，用手指轻轻拂去上面的灰尘，那痕迹果然是血迹，虽然已经干涸发黑，但依旧能看出是新鲜不久的。他又仔细检查了一番，发现血迹顺着佛像的底座，一直延伸到殿后的角落，角落里堆放着一些残破的佛像碎片和腐朽的木材，遮挡住了一部分视线。
就在他准备拨开碎片，一探究竟时，身后突然传来一阵轻微的脚步声，“嗒、嗒、嗒”，节奏缓慢而沉重，像是有人穿着厚重的鞋子，在殿内行走。萧琰猛地回头，殿内空无一人，只有阳光透过破洞，在地面上投下斑驳的光影，那脚步声却戛然而止，仿佛从未出现过一般。
“是谁？”萧琰低喝一声，声音在空旷的大殿内回荡，没有任何回应。他握紧软剑，缓缓转过身，目光警惕地扫视着殿内的每一个角落，佛像的阴影、残破的香案、堆积的碎片，每一处都可能隐藏着危险。他知道，这灵泉寺绝非表面看起来这般简单，失踪的李大人、失踪的差役，还有这诡异的血迹和脚步声，都在暗示着这里藏着不为人知的秘密，藏着吞噬生命的凶煞。
萧琰定了定神，压下心中的寒意，继续探查。他拨开殿后角落的碎片，发现里面竟然有一个狭窄的通道，通道口被一块破旧的木板挡住，木板上布满了抓痕，还有几滴未干涸的血迹，显然是不久前有人从这里经过。通道内一片漆黑，散发着浓重的霉味和血腥气，让人窒息。
他从怀中掏出火折子，吹亮后，小心翼翼地走进通道。通道很窄，只能容一人通过，两侧的墙壁湿漉漉的，上面布满了青苔，脚下的地面也十分湿滑，一不小心就会摔倒。火折子的光芒微弱，只能照亮身前几步远的地方，通道内的黑暗仿佛无穷无尽，像是一张巨大的嘴巴，要将他吞噬。
走了约莫十几步，通道豁然开朗，眼前出现了一个小小的石室。石室的墙壁上，刻着一些诡异的符文，符文是用朱砂书写，颜色鲜红，像是刚写上去的，隐隐散发着一股阴邪的气息。石室的中央，摆放着一个石桌，石桌上放着一个残破的陶罐，陶罐里装着一些暗红色的液体，散发着刺鼻的血腥气，旁边还有几枚刻着诡异图案的铜牌，与山脚下发现的那枚“灵泉”令牌样式相似，只是上面的图案更加狰狞。
石桌的旁边，躺着一具尸体，尸体穿着青色的官袍，正是失踪的御史李大人。李大人的双目圆睁，脸上布满了惊恐的神色，仿佛在临死前看到了极其恐怖的东西，他的脖颈处有一道深深的伤口，伤口边缘整齐，显然是被利器所伤，鲜血早已干涸，染红了身前的官袍。尸体的手中，紧紧攥着半张残破的纸，纸上写着几行模糊的字迹，依稀能辨认出“凶煞”“祭祀”“灵泉”等字样。
萧琰蹲下身，小心翼翼地掰开李大人的手指，取出那张残破的纸。纸张已经泛黄，上面的字迹潦草而凌乱，显然是李大人在临死前仓促写下的。除了那几个模糊的字样，还有一些断断续续的句子：“灵泉寺有凶煞，以人血祭祀……僧人诡异，并非真僧……令牌藏秘密……”后面的字迹被血迹覆盖，再也无法辨认。
就在这时，石室的入口处突然传来一阵低沉的笑声，笑声阴冷而诡异，不似人声，像是某种野兽的低吼，又像是亡魂的狞笑。“桀桀桀……又来一个送死的……”

萧琰猛地站起身，握紧软剑，目光投向入口处。只见一个身穿灰色僧袍的人，缓缓走了进来，那人头戴僧帽，帽檐压得很低，遮住了面容，只能看到嘴角露出的诡异笑容，他的脚步轻盈，落地无声，身上散发着与石室中相同的阴邪气息。
“你是谁？”萧琰沉声问道，声音中带着一丝冷意。他能感觉到，眼前这个人绝非普通的僧人，他的气息阴冷，眼神中透着凶光，显然就是李大人笔下的“凶煞”，或是与凶煞有关的人。
那人没有回答，只是缓缓抬起头，帽檐下露出一张扭曲的脸——脸色惨白如纸，没有一丝血色，双眼是浑浊的黑色，没有眼白，嘴角咧开的弧度极大，露出尖锐的牙齿，像是野兽一般。“桀桀桀……我是谁？我是守护灵泉寺的神……你们这些闯入者，都得死……”
话音刚落，那人猛地扑了过来，速度快得惊人，手中不知何时多了一把锋利的短刀，短刀上闪烁着寒光，还沾着暗红色的血迹。萧琰早有防备，侧身避开，软剑瞬间出鞘，“唰”的一声，剑刃划破空气，朝着那人刺去。
那人反应极快，侧身避开软剑，短刀带着风声，朝着萧琰的脖颈划来。萧琰弯腰躲闪，同时抬脚踹向那人的腹部，那人被踹中，踉跄着后退了几步，眼中的凶光更盛。“不知死活的东西，竟敢反抗……”
两人在狭小的石室中缠斗起来，软剑的灵动与短刀的狠厉交织在一起，发出“叮叮当当”的碰撞声。萧琰的剑法精湛，招招致命，却发现那人的身手极为诡异，不似寻常武林人士，动作僵硬，却力大无穷，而且不怕疼痛，即使被软剑划伤，也没有丝毫反应，依旧疯狂地扑上来。
缠斗中，萧琰注意到那人的僧袍下，露出了一截青黑色的皮肤，皮肤上布满了诡异的符文，与石室墙壁上的符文一模一样。他心中一动，想起李大人纸上写的“以人血祭祀”，看来眼前这个人，或许是被某种邪术控制，变成了不人不鬼的凶煞，而灵泉寺的僧人，恐怕也都参与其中，用活人祭祀，炼制邪术。
就在这时，那人突然发出一声凄厉的嘶吼，身体猛地膨胀起来，皮肤变得更加青黑，双眼也变成了血红色，手中的短刀也变得更加锋利。“受死吧！”他嘶吼着，再次扑了过来，短刀直刺萧琰的胸口。
萧琰眼神一凛，不退反进，软剑挽起一个剑花，避开短刀的同时，狠狠刺向那人胸口的符文。“噗嗤”一声，软剑刺穿了那人的胸口，符文被破坏，那人发出一声凄厉的惨叫，身体开始抽搐，青黑色的皮肤渐渐褪去，露出底下正常的肤色，只是眼神依旧浑浊，显然已经没了气息。
萧琰拔出软剑，剑刃上的血迹滴落，落在石室的地面上，与地上的血迹交融在一起。他喘了口气，刚才的缠斗耗费了他不少体力，虽然解决了眼前的凶煞，但他知道，这灵泉寺的危机远未解除。李大人纸上写的“僧人诡异”，说明寺中还有其他的凶煞，而那所谓的“祭祀”，恐怕还在继续。
他收起软剑，目光再次投向石室的墙壁，那些诡异的符文依旧散发着阴邪的气息，石桌上的陶罐和铜牌，也透着不寻常的诡异。他拿起一枚铜牌，仔细观察，铜牌上的图案是一个狰狞的恶鬼，恶鬼的手中捧着一口泉水，正是灵泉寺的“灵泉”。他忽然想起，灵泉寺之所以得名，是因为寺中有一口灵泉，传说喝了灵泉的水，能消灾解难，可如今看来，这灵泉恐怕早已被邪术污染，变成了滋养凶煞的工具。
萧琰又检查了一番李大人的尸体，发现他的腰间少了一块令牌，想必就是那枚刻着“灵泉”二字的铜令牌，或许是被寺中的僧人拿走了。他将李大人的尸体轻轻挪到一旁，用石块盖住，心中默念：“李大人，放心，我定会查明真相，为你和失踪的人报仇。”
随后，他拿起火折子，转身走出石室，沿着通道回到大雄宝殿。此时，殿外的雾气更加浓重，风也变得更加猛烈，殿檐下的残破灯笼摇晃得愈发厉害，像是在预示着更大的危险。萧琰知道，他不能停留，必须尽快找到其他的线索，查明灵泉寺的秘密，阻止那诡异的祭祀，彻底铲除寺中的凶煞。
他走出大雄宝殿，目光扫视着庭院两侧的配殿。左侧是伽蓝殿，右侧是祖师殿，两座配殿的门都紧紧关着，门上布满了蛛网和灰尘，看起来已经荒废了很久。萧琰犹豫了片刻，决定先去伽蓝殿看看，或许能找到一些线索。
他走到伽蓝殿门口，抬手推了推门，门纹丝不动，显然是被锁住了。他从怀中掏出一把小巧的匕首，小心翼翼地插入锁孔，轻轻转动，“咔哒”一声，锁被打开了。推开殿门，一股比大雄宝殿更浓重的霉味和血腥气扑面而来，殿内一片漆黑，比大雄宝殿还要昏暗。
萧琰吹亮火折子，走进伽蓝殿。殿内的伽蓝菩萨像早已残破不堪，倒在地上，身上布满了灰尘和裂痕。殿内的地面上，散落着几具骸骨，骸骨的穿着各不相同，有僧人的僧袍，有普通人的布衣，还有官差的服饰，显然是失踪的差役和其他闯入者。骸骨的身上，都有明显的伤痕，有的脖颈断裂，有的胸口被刺穿，死状凄惨，显然是被凶煞所害。
萧琰的目光缓缓扫过骸骨，忽然注意到一具骸骨的手中，紧紧攥着一枚铜令牌，正是李大人失踪的那枚“灵泉”令牌。他走过去，小心翼翼地掰开骸骨的手指，取出令牌。令牌上除了“灵泉”二字，背面还刻着一些诡异的符文，与石室墙壁上的符文相似，只是更加简洁。
就在他仔细观察令牌的时候，身后突然传来一阵脚步声，这次的脚步声不止一个，杂乱而沉重，朝着伽蓝殿的方向走来。萧琰猛地回头，握紧了腰间的软剑，目光警惕地望向殿门口。只见几个身穿灰色僧袍的人，缓缓走了进来，他们的面容都被帽檐遮住，身上散发着阴邪的气息，与刚才在石室中遇到的凶煞一模一样。
“桀桀桀……看来你发现了不少秘密啊……”为首的僧人开口，声音阴冷而沙哑，不似人声。“既然来了，就别想走了，乖乖成为祭祀的祭品吧……”
萧琰眼神一冷，手中的软剑再次出鞘，寒光闪烁。他知道，一场更激烈的战斗即将开始，而这灵泉寺的凶煞之谜，也将在这场刀刃相交的较量中，逐渐揭开神秘的面纱。他深吸一口气，调整好呼吸，目光紧紧盯着眼前的僧人，心中只有一个念头：刃破万重迷，誓要将这古寺中的凶煞彻底铲除，还世间一片清明。

The late autumn wind swept the dead leaves on the mountain and swirled on the rugged mountain path. Xiao Yan reined in the reins, and the green-maned horse under his crotch paved its hooves uneasily, white breath exhaling from its nose, and looking warily into the depths of the dense forest. Ahead, there are clouds and mist, and you can vaguely see the cornices piercing the mist. That is Lingquan Temple - an ancient temple hidden deep in Cangwu Mountain that has been abandoned for more than ten years.
His trip was to track down Mr. Li, the censor who disappeared three months ago. According to the woodcutter who last saw Mr. Li, he and his party of five entered the mountain in the direction of Lingquan Temple, and there has been no news since then. The government once sent people to search the mountain, but they only found half a blood-stained fragment of an official robe and a copper token engraved with the word "Lingquan" at the foot of the mountain. No other clues were found. What's even weirder is that two of the policemen who searched the mountain disappeared inexplicably, and the rest of them all looked pale. They claimed that they heard shrill cries coming from the direction of the ancient temple at night, and saw black shadows shuttling in the forest, and they dared not go even half a step deeper.
Xiao Yan raised his hand and took hold of the soft sword at his waist. The scabbard was made of dark iron and engraved with fine cloud patterns. It was slightly cool in his hand. He had practiced martial arts since he was a child, and had served in the Ministry of Justice for several years. He had seen countless murder scenes, but he had never been as depressed as he was now by the cold atmosphere in the mountains. Cangwu Mountain is already high and densely forested, but it becomes even more deserted after autumn. The only sound of the wind rustling through the leaves, mixed with the low calls of unknown birds and beasts in the distance, makes it even more lonely and terrifying.
"Drive." Xiao Yan shouted softly and patted the horse's neck. Although the green-maned horse was still afraid, it still walked obediently on the dead leaves and walked slowly deeper into the clouds and mist. The closer we got to Lingquan Temple, the thicker the mist became. Visibility was less than ten feet, and a strange smell gradually filled the air - a damp musty smell, a faint sandalwood smell, and a hint of blood. The three were intertwined and made people sick.
About half an hour later, the mountain gate of Lingquan Temple finally appeared in front of you. The mountain gate is made of bluestone and is more than three feet high. The glazed tiles on the top have long been mottled and peeled off, revealing the dark blue bricks underneath. The stone lions on both sides are also incomplete, one has a missing head and the other has a broken front paw. Their ferocious faces look even more sinister in the mist. The three characters "Lingquan Temple" above the mountain gate were written in cinnabar. Now most of the cinnabar has peeled off, leaving only a vague outline, as if eroded by time and some strange force.
Xiao Yan turned over and dismounted, and tied the horse to the old locust tree next to the mountain gate. The old locust tree had long since died, and its branches were twisted like ghost claws, entangled with dry vines, like countless pairs of outstretched hands, dragging people into the darkness. He raised his hand and pushed the mountain door. "Creak!" A long and harsh sound broke the silence of the mountain. This sound echoed in the empty valley, with a hint of crying, making people's scalp numb. The mountain door was not locked, but was sealed by thick cobwebs and dust. When pushed, the dust fell, mixed with a few frightened black spiders, and fled in a hurry.
The moment he stepped into the mountain gate, a biting chill hit his face. It was completely different from the autumn wind in the mountains. This chill was a bit sinister, as if it could penetrate clothes and freeze into the bone marrow. Xiao Yan subconsciously clenched the soft sword at his waist and scanned the surroundings with vigilance. Inside the mountain gate is an open courtyard. The ground is covered with thick dead leaves and weeds. Several withered ancient cypresses stand on both sides of the courtyard, their branches slanting toward the sky, as if they are silently complaining. There is a stone incense burner in the center of the courtyard. The furnace body is full of cracks. There is no incense inside, only some blackened ashes are left. A few broken pieces of cloth can be vaguely seen in the ashes. The color is dark, as if it has been stained with blood.
At the end of the courtyard is the main hall of Lingquan Temple, the Main Hall. The door of the main hall was ajar, and the red paint on the door panel had peeled off, revealing the wooden texture underneath, which was covered with scratches, as if it had been scratched repeatedly by something sharp. The lanterns under the eaves of the palace have long since decayed, only the broken skeleton is left, swaying gently in the wind, making a "clattering" sound, like the whisper of the dead soul.
Xiao Yan slowed down and walked towards the Main Hall step by step. The dead leaves under his feet made a "clicking" sound, which was particularly clear in the silent courtyard. With every step he took, he could feel the sinister aura in the air getting stronger and stronger, and the bloody aura becoming clearer, as if it was coming from the Great Hall. When he reached the entrance of the palace, he stopped and listened. There was dead silence in the palace, without any sound, but it seemed as if there were countless pairs of eyes staring at him in the dark, making the hair on his body stand on end.
He took a deep breath, raised his hand and gently pushed open the palace door. "Creak -" There was another harsh sound, and the light in the hall instantly became dim. Only a few rays of sunlight slanted in through the holes in the roof of the hall, illuminating the dust flying in the air. Xiao Yan adapted for a moment and then gradually saw the scene in the palace clearly.
In the main hall, the statue of Sakyamuni Buddha in the middle has long been mutilated. The Buddha's head is missing, the body is covered with cracks, and one of his hands is broken. Only the empty sleeves are left, as if he is crying silently. On the incense table in front of the Buddha statue, there are three broken incense burners, which are covered with dust. There are also a few rusty copper coins and half broken candles scattered on the incense table. The walls of the hall were originally painted with exquisite murals, but now they have been painted beyond recognition, leaving only some blurred lines. It can be vaguely seen as scenes from Buddhist scriptures, but the faces of the characters have been painted to look ferocious, and their eyes are weird, as if they are coming out of the wall.
Xiao Yan's eyes slowly swept across the hall, and suddenly he noticed a trace of dark red under the base of the Buddha statue, like dried blood. He walked over quickly, squatted down, and gently brushed off the dust on it with his fingers. The trace was indeed blood. Although it had dried and turned black, it could still be seen that it was fresh. He checked carefully again and found that the blood stains extended along the base of the Buddha statue to the corner at the back of the hall. There were some broken Buddha statue fragments and rotten wood piled in the corner, blocking part of the view.
Just when he was about to open up the fragments and take a closer look, there was a sudden sound of footsteps behind him, "ta, ta, ta". The rhythm was slow and heavy, as if someone was wearing heavy shoes and walking in the temple. Xiao Yan turned around suddenly. There was no one in the hall. Only the sunlight filtered through the holes, casting mottled light and shadow on the ground. The footsteps stopped suddenly, as if they had never appeared.
"Who is it?" Xiao Yan shouted in a low voice, his voice echoing in the empty hall without any response. He gripped the soft sword tightly, turned around slowly, and scanned every corner of the hall with vigilant eyes. The shadow of the Buddha statue, the broken incense table, and the piled up debris could hide dangers everywhere. He knew that Lingquan Temple was not as simple as it seemed on the surface. The missing Master Li, the missing servant, and the strange blood stains and footsteps all hinted that there were unknown secrets hidden here, and there was a vicious evil that devoured lives.
Xiao Yan calmed down, suppressed the chill in his heart, and continued to investigate. He pushed aside the debris in the back corner of the hall and found that there was a narrow passage inside. The entrance of the passage was blocked by an old wooden board. The board was covered with scratches and a few drops of undried blood. It was obvious that someone had passed here not long ago. The passage was pitch black, exuding a strong smell of mold and blood that was suffocating.
He took out the fire stick from his arms, blew it brightly, and walked carefully into the passage. The passage is very narrow and can only accommodate one person. The walls on both sides are wet and covered with moss. The ground under your feet is also very slippery. If you are not careful, you will fall. Huo Zhezi's light was weak and could only illuminate a few steps in front of him. The darkness in the passage seemed endless, like a huge mouth that wanted to swallow him up.
Gone for about a whileAfter more than ten steps, the passage suddenly opened up, and a small stone chamber appeared in front of me. There were some strange runes carved on the walls of the stone chamber. The runes were written in cinnabar and were bright red in color, as if they had just been written on them. They exuded a faint evil aura. In the center of the stone room, there is a stone table. On the stone table is a broken clay pot. The pot is filled with some dark red liquid, exuding a pungent smell of blood. Next to it are several bronze medals engraved with strange patterns. They are similar in style to the "Spiritual Spring" token found at the foot of the mountain, but the patterns on it are more ferocious.
Next to the stone table, there was a corpse lying. The corpse was wearing a blue official robe. It was the missing Censor Li. Mr. Li's eyes were wide open, and his face was filled with a look of horror, as if he had seen something extremely terrifying before he died. There was a deep wound on his neck with neat edges. It was obviously injured by a sharp weapon. The blood had long dried up and dyed the official robe in front of him red. In the hands of the corpse, there was a half piece of torn paper tightly clutched. There were a few lines of vague handwriting written on the paper, and the words "fierce", "sacrifice" and "spiritual spring" could be vaguely discerned.
Xiao Yan knelt down, carefully opened Master Li's fingers, and took out the torn piece of paper. The paper was yellowed, and the handwriting on it was scrawled and messy. It was obviously written hastily by Mr. Li before his death. In addition to those few vague words, there are also some intermittent sentences: "There is a fierce evil in Lingquan Temple, and human blood is used to sacrifice... The monk is weird, not a real monk... The token hides secrets..." The writing behind it was covered with blood and could no longer be read.
At this moment, a low laughter suddenly came from the entrance of the stone chamber. The laughter was cold and strange. It was not like a human voice, but like the low roar of some kind of wild beast or the grin of a dead soul. "Jie Jie Jie... Another one is here to die..."
Xiao Yan stood up suddenly, gripped the soft sword tightly, and looked at the entrance. I saw a man wearing a gray monk's robe slowly walking in. The man wore a monk's hat with a low brim, covering his face. Only the weird smile could be seen at the corner of his mouth. His steps were light and he landed silently. He exuded the same sinister aura as in the stone chamber.
"Who are you?" Xiao Yan asked in a deep voice, with a hint of coldness in his voice. He could feel that the man in front of him was no ordinary monk. His aura was cold and there was a fierce light in his eyes. He was obviously the "fierce evil spirit" described by Mr. Li, or someone related to the evil evil spirit.
The man did not answer, but slowly raised his head, revealing a twisted face under the brim of his hat - his face was as pale as paper, without a trace of blood, his eyes were turbid black, with no whites, and the corners of his mouth were wide open, revealing sharp teeth, like a wild beast. "Jiejiejie...who am I? I am the god who protects Lingquan Temple...all of you intruders must die..."
As soon as he finished speaking, the man rushed over at an astonishing speed. At some point, there was a sharp dagger in his hand. The dagger flashed with cold light and was stained with dark red blood. Xiao Yan was already on guard, and turned sideways to avoid it. The soft sword was instantly unsheathed, and with a "swish" sound, the blade cut through the air and stabbed towards the man.
The man reacted very quickly and turned sideways to avoid the soft sword. The short knife made a sound of wind and slashed towards Xiao Yan's neck. Xiao Yan bent down to dodge, and at the same time raised his foot to kick the man in the abdomen. The man was kicked and staggered back a few steps, the fierce light in his eyes getting stronger. "How dare you resist..."
The two of them fought in the small stone room. The flexibility of the soft sword and the sharpness of the short sword intertwined, making a "clinking" collision sound. Xiao Yan's swordsmanship was exquisite and his moves were deadly, but he found that the man's skills were extremely strange. He was not like ordinary martial arts people. His movements were stiff, but he was extremely powerful. He was not afraid of pain. Even if he was scratched by a soft sword, he did not react at all and still pounced on him crazily.
During the fight, Xiao Yan noticed that a section of blue-black skin was exposed under the man's monk's robe.His skin was covered with strange runes, which were exactly the same as those on the walls of the stone chamber. With a thought in his mind, he remembered the "sacrifice with human blood" written on Master Li's paper. It seemed that the man in front of him might have been controlled by some kind of evil magic and turned into a vicious evil that was neither human nor ghost. The monks of Lingquan Temple were probably also involved, using human sacrifices to refine the evil magic.
At this moment, the man suddenly let out a shrill roar, his body suddenly swelled, his skin became darker, his eyes turned blood red, and the short knife in his hand became sharper. "Suffer death!" He roared and rushed over again, stabbing Xiao Yan's chest with the short knife.
Xiao Yan's eyes were sharp, and he advanced instead of retreating. He picked up a sword flower with his soft sword, avoided the short sword, and stabbed the rune on the man's chest fiercely. With a "poof" sound, the soft sword pierced the man's chest, and the runes were destroyed. The man let out a shrill scream, and his body began to twitch. The blue-black skin gradually faded away, revealing the normal skin color underneath, but his eyes were still cloudy, and he had obviously lost his breath.
Xiao Yan pulled out the soft sword, and the blood on the blade dripped and fell on the ground of the stone room, blending with the blood on the ground. He took a breath. The struggle just now consumed a lot of his energy. Although he had solved the evil in front of him, he knew that the crisis in Lingquan Temple was far from over. The "monk is weird" written on Master Li's paper indicates that there are other evil spirits in the temple, and the so-called "sacrifice" is probably still going on.
He put away the soft sword and cast his gaze on the wall of the stone room again. The strange runes still exuded an evil aura, and the pottery pots and bronze medals on the stone table also exuded unusual weirdness. He picked up a bronze medal and observed it carefully. The pattern on the bronze medal was a ferocious evil ghost. The evil ghost was holding a spring in his hand, which was the "Lingquan" of Lingquan Temple. He suddenly remembered that Lingquan Temple got its name because there was a spiritual spring in the temple. Legend has it that drinking the water from the spiritual spring can ward off disasters and solve problems. But now it seems that this spiritual spring may have been polluted by evil magic and turned into a tool for nourishing evil spirits.
Xiao Yan checked Mr. Li's body again and found that a token was missing from his waist. It must be the copper token with the word "Lingquan" engraved on it. Perhaps it was taken away by the monks in the temple. He gently moved Lord Li's body aside, covered it with stones, and said silently in his heart: "Don't worry, Lord Li, I will definitely find out the truth and avenge you and the missing people."
Then, he picked up the fire seal, turned around and walked out of the stone room, and returned to the main hall along the passage. At this time, the fog outside the palace became thicker, the wind became more violent, and the broken lantern under the eaves of the palace swayed more violently, as if foreshadowing a greater danger. Xiao Yan knew that he could not stay and must find other clues as soon as possible to find out the secret of Lingquan Temple, stop the weird sacrifice, and completely eradicate the evil in the temple.
He walked out of the main hall and glanced at the side halls on both sides of the courtyard. On the left is the Jialan Hall, and on the right is the Patriarch Hall. The doors of the two side halls are tightly closed. The doors are covered with cobwebs and dust, and they look like they have been abandoned for a long time. Xiao Yan hesitated for a moment and decided to go to Jialan Hall first, maybe he could find some clues.
He walked to the door of Jialan Hall, raised his hand and pushed the door. The door didn't move at all, it was obviously locked. He took out a small dagger from his arms, carefully inserted it into the keyhole, turned it gently, and with a "click" the lock was opened. Pushing open the door of the palace, a smell of mustiness and blood that was stronger than that of the Mahavira Palace hit my face. The interior of the palace was pitch black, even darker than the Mahavira Palace.
Xiao Yan blew a bright fire tune and walked into Jialan Hall. The statue of Jialan Bodhisattva in the hall had long been broken and fell to the ground, covered with dust and cracks. There are several skeletons scattered on the ground in the hall. The skeletons are dressed in different clothes. Some are monks' robes, some ordinary people's clothes, and some officials' clothes. They are obviously missing officials and other intruders. on the skeleton, all had obvious injuries, some had broken necks, some had their chests pierced, and their deaths were miserable, obviously caused by evil spirits.
Xiao Yan's eyes slowly swept over the skeletons, and suddenly he noticed that in the hand of a skeleton, there was a copper token tightly clutched, which was the "Spiritual Spring" token that Mr. Li had lost. He walked over, carefully opened the skeleton's fingers, and took out the token. In addition to the word "spiritual spring" on the token, there are also some strange runes engraved on the back, which are similar to the runes on the walls of the stone chamber, but more concise.
Just as he was carefully observing the token, a burst of footsteps suddenly came from behind him. This time there were more than one footsteps, messy and heavy, walking towards the direction of Jialan Palace. Xiao Yan turned around suddenly, grasped the soft sword at his waist, and looked at the entrance of the palace warily. I saw a few people wearing gray monk robes slowly walking in. Their faces were covered by the brim of their hats, and they exuded an evil aura, exactly the same as the evil spirits they encountered in the stone chamber just now.
"Jie Jie Jie... It seems you have discovered a lot of secrets..." The leading monk spoke, his voice cold and hoarse, not like a human voice. "Now that you're here, don't even think about leaving. Just become a sacrifice for the sacrifice..."
Xiao Yan's eyes turned cold, and the soft sword in his hand was unsheathed again, its cold light flashing. He knew that a more intense battle was about to begin, and the mystery of the evil in Lingquan Temple would gradually be revealed in this sword-blade battle. He took a deep breath, adjusted his breathing, and stared at the monk in front of him. He had only one thought in his mind: to break through all the mystery, vow to completely eradicate the evil spirits in this ancient temple, and restore clarity to the world.
